quests.instruction: A new library will be built on a sloping site. Before the building is drawn, who measures the land's size, boundaries, and slope?
quests.hint: Think about measuring the ground, not designing rooms.
quests.explanation: Land surveyors measure land so designers know what space and slope they have. Decorators style rooms, and inspectors check finished work.
quests.funFact: Surveyors often use instruments that measure angles and distances very precisely.

quests.instruction: A ward patient needs their temperature checked every hour, and their medicine checked against the prescription. Which pair matches the two tasks?
options: Porter for temperature, cleaner for medicine
Receptionist for temperature, surgeon for medicine
Nurse for temperature, pharmacist for medicine
quests.correctAnswer: Nurse for temperature, pharmacist for medicine
quests.hint: Match each task to someone trained in it.
quests.explanation: Nurses monitor patients on the ward, and pharmacists check and prepare medicines. The other pairs do not match the training needed.
quests.funFact: Hospitals often rely on several kinds of trained workers, each with a different focus.

quests.instruction: Both translators and interpreters work with languages. What mainly separates them?
options: Translators work with written words; interpreters speak aloud
Translators handle live speech; interpreters only handle books
Translators write dictionaries; interpreters write songs
quests.correctAnswer: Translators work with written words; interpreters speak aloud
quests.hint: Think about paper versus spoken conversation.
quests.explanation: Translators turn written text into another language, while interpreters help people understand speech as it happens.
quests.funFact: Interpreters at big meetings sometimes work in pairs so they can take turns and rest.

quests.instruction: Which tool pair suits a marine biologist counting coral and an astronomer studying distant stars?
quests.hint: Match each scientist's tool to where they look.
quests.explanation: Coral lives underwater, so a marine biologist needs an underwater camera, and distant stars call for a telescope. The swapped pair reverses them.
quests.funFact: Telescopes gather faint light so that far-off objects can be seen more clearly.

quests.instruction: A bakery wants to know why its bread turns out dense. How might a food scientist approach the problem?
options: Taste the bread and decide very quickly
Test one change at a time in experiments
Change the menu and repaint the whole shop
quests.correctAnswer: Test one change at a time in experiments
quests.hint: Think about changing one thing at a time and recording what happens.
quests.explanation: Food scientists test one factor at a time, so they can see what truly affects the bread.
quests.funFact: Controlled experiments change just one thing at a time so results can be compared fairly.

quests.instruction: Which doctor is trained to read X-rays, scans, and similar images to help find problems?
quests.hint: Think about a doctor who works with pictures of the inside of the body.
quests.explanation: Radiologists study medical images to help find injuries or illnesses. Anesthetists manage pain during procedures, and dermatologists focus on skin.
quests.funFact: Some scans use sound waves or magnets instead of X-rays.

quests.instruction: A museum painting has faded and cracked. Which expert cleans and repairs it carefully without changing the artist's work?
quests.hint: Think about careful repair that respects the original.
quests.explanation: Restorers use gentle methods to preserve artworks. Guards protect them, and framers make frames.
quests.funFact: Art restorers often keep detailed notes and photos of every step they take.

quests.instruction: Engineers worry about cracks in an old bridge. Who studies how the bridge carries weight and decides if it is safe?
quests.hint: Think about someone who understands forces inside buildings and bridges.
quests.explanation: Structural engineers study how structures carry loads and spot weaknesses. Wardens manage traffic, and painters protect surfaces.
quests.funFact: Many bridges are inspected regularly so small problems can be fixed early.

quests.instruction: A school has a deaf student who communicates by signing. Which professional helps lessons make sense in real time?
quests.hint: Think about someone who turns spoken lessons into signs.
quests.explanation: Sign language interpreters pass on spoken words in signs as lessons happen. A radio host and a library assistant do not.
quests.funFact: Sign languages have their own grammar and are different in different countries.

quests.instruction: If nobody checked fridge temperatures in a food factory, what might happen?
options: The factory would make food faster
Food could spoil and make people unwell
Customers would always get cheaper food
quests.correctAnswer: Food could spoil and make people unwell
quests.hint: Think about what warm conditions do to some foods.
quests.explanation: Cold storage slows the growth of germs. Without checks, food may spoil unnoticed and cause illness.
quests.funFact: Many food makers record fridge temperatures regularly to show that food stayed cold.

quests.instruction: A pilot skips the pre-flight checklist. Why is this a problem?
options: A fault might be missed before takeoff
The plane would automatically land sooner
Passengers would get more luggage space
quests.correctAnswer: A fault might be missed before takeoff
quests.hint: Think about what a checklist is designed to catch.
quests.explanation: Checklists help pilots spot problems early, when they are easiest to fix. Skipping them can let a fault slip by.
quests.funFact: Checklists are used in many jobs, including surgery and building work.

quests.instruction: A lifeguard leaves the pool chair to chat with friends. What could go wrong?
options: The water would become much deeper
The pool would close at lunchtime
A swimmer in trouble may go unseen
quests.correctAnswer: A swimmer in trouble may go unseen
quests.hint: Think about why lifeguards watch the water constantly.
quests.explanation: A lifeguard's main job is to watch swimmers, so leaving the post can delay help.
quests.funFact: Lifeguards often rotate positions to stay alert during long shifts.

quests.instruction: A new school is being built. Which order of jobs makes the most sense?
quests.hint: Think about measuring first and checking last.
quests.explanation: The land is measured first, the building designed next, then built, and finally checked for safety.
quests.funFact: Many building projects have inspections at several stages, not only at the end.

quests.instruction: A town wants a new bus route. Which order of helpers makes the most sense?
options: Bus driver, road engineer, transport planner
Road engineer, bus driver, transport planner
Transport planner, road engineer, bus driver
quests.correctAnswer: Transport planner, road engineer, bus driver
quests.hint: Think about planning before building and driving.
quests.explanation: Planners choose where buses should go, engineers prepare the roads, and drivers run the service.
quests.funFact: Planners often count how many people travel along a route before choosing bus stops.

quests.instruction: A hospital kitchen prepares meals for patients with different health needs. Who advises which foods suit each patient?
quests.hint: Think about an expert in food and health.
quests.explanation: Clinical nutritionists use knowledge of nutrition and health to advise on meals. Critics review food, and porters help move supplies.
quests.funFact: Some patients need meals with less salt or sugar, depending on their health.

quests.instruction: A football referee must treat both teams in exactly the same way. Which value does this show?
quests.hint: Think about equal treatment for everyone.
quests.explanation: Fairness means applying the rules equally to everyone, which is the heart of a referee's role.
quests.funFact: Referees use hand signals so players and fans can understand decisions in a noisy stadium.

quests.instruction: A journalist hears an exciting rumor. What should they do before writing it?
options: Print it quickly to be first
Ask friends if it sounds fun
quests.hint: Think about proving something before sharing it.
quests.explanation: Good reporters confirm facts with trustworthy sources so readers are not misled.
quests.funFact: Many news organizations have editors who help check facts before stories are published.

quests.instruction: A doctor hears private health details from a patient. What should the doctor do with this information?
options: Keep it private unless safety requires sharing
Share it with any neighbor who asks politely
Post it in a public group to teach others
quests.correctAnswer: Keep it private unless safety requires sharing
quests.hint: Think about trust between a patient and a doctor.
quests.explanation: Keeping health details private builds trust, and sharing is limited to what care or safety needs.
quests.funFact: Many countries have laws that protect the privacy of health records.

quests.instruction: Solar panels are being fitted to a school roof. Which worker usually installs the panels and checks the wiring safely?
quests.hint: Think about roofs, sunlight, and electricity.
quests.explanation: Solar panel installers fix panels in place and connect them safely. Sweeps and cleaners do different jobs.
quests.funFact: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity, even on some cloudy days.

quests.instruction: A factory robot arm stops in the middle of a shift. Which worker diagnoses and repairs it?
quests.hint: Think about someone who understands machines with moving arms and sensors.
quests.explanation: Robotics technicians find faults in robots and fix them. Cleaners and cashiers do other work.
quests.funFact: Many factory robots repeat the same task precisely, so a small fault can stop the whole line.

quests.instruction: A 3D printer will make a model of a new tool. Who first designs the shape on a computer?
quests.hint: Think about who plans how products look and work.
quests.explanation: Industrial designers plan shapes and features before products are made. Cleaners and couriers have other jobs.
quests.funFact: A 3D printer builds objects by adding material in thin layers.

quests.instruction: Which job is most likely to involve night shifts to keep an important service running?
quests.hint: Think about services people need at any hour.
quests.explanation: Hospitals work around the clock, so many nurses work nights. Museums and schools usually keep daytime hours.
quests.funFact: Many emergency services and hospitals run all night.

quests.instruction: A job is mostly outdoors, changes with the seasons, and involves caring for crops and land. Which fits best?
quests.hint: Think about a job that follows the seasons.
quests.explanation: Arable farmers grow crops and follow the seasons. Clerks and call center agents usually work indoors.
quests.funFact: Many farmers plan planting and harvest times around the weather.

quests.instruction: Two jobs both need teamwork. Which one depends most on exact timing between people backstage?
quests.hint: Think about cues and changes during a live show.
quests.explanation: Stage managers call cues so lights, sound, and actors work together at the right moment.
quests.funFact: Stage managers often follow a script marked with cues for each change.

quests.instruction: A city worries about heavy rain flooding its streets. Which combination of experts works best on a solution?
options: Hydrologist, pastry chef, and sign painter
Civil engineer, florist, and tour guide
quests.hint: Think about water, construction, and town planning.
quests.explanation: Hydrologists study water, civil engineers build drains and barriers, and planners decide where and how to build.
quests.funFact: Some cities add parks and green spaces that soak up extra rainwater.

quests.instruction: A school wants to start a vegetable garden. Which group of helpers fits best?
options: A gardener, a pilot, and a drummer
A gardener, a teacher, and a parent
A teacher, a dentist, and a bank manager
quests.correctAnswer: A gardener, a teacher, and a parent
quests.hint: Think about people who know plants, learning, and local help.
quests.explanation: A gardener knows plants, a teacher plans learning, and a parent offers help. The other groups have missing skills.
quests.funFact: School gardens can be used to teach children about plants, weather, and food.

quests.instruction: An old village hall must be made easy to enter for wheelchair users. Who should plan the ramps and doorways?
quests.hint: Think about someone who studies how buildings welcome everyone.
quests.explanation: Access consultants advise on ramps, wide doors, and layouts so more people can use a building.
quests.funFact: A gentle ramp is usually longer than a steep one, which makes it easier to use.

quests.instruction: Why do communities need so many different jobs?
options: Because most jobs are exactly the same
No single worker can do every task well
So that no one ever needs to cooperate
quests.correctAnswer: No single worker can do every task well
quests.hint: Think about how many skills are needed to run a town.
quests.explanation: Different jobs bring different skills, so people can rely on one another for what they cannot do alone.
quests.funFact: Some jobs, such as building a bridge, can involve hundreds of workers.

quests.instruction: Which pair shows two jobs that depend on each other?
options: A farmer grows wheat, and a baker uses it
A baker bakes bread, and an actor sings opera
A pilot flies planes, and a florist writes code
quests.correctAnswer: A farmer grows wheat, and a baker uses it
quests.hint: Look for one worker's output becoming another's ingredient.
quests.explanation: Wheat grown by a farmer can become flour that a baker uses, which links the two jobs.
quests.funFact: Flour is made by milling grains such as wheat.

quests.instruction: To choose a career, which approach best combines everything you have learned?
options: Choose only the job with the shortest name in town
Pick the first job you see on a poster
Explore interests, build skills, talk to workers
quests.correctAnswer: Explore interests, build skills, talk to workers
quests.hint: Think about learning from real people and trying things.
quests.explanation: Careers fit best when interests, skills, and real experience come together. Short names and posters say little about a job.
quests.funFact: Many people change careers during their lives as they learn new skills.
